title: Tryb przypuszczający · -bym, -byś, -by
note: B1 Block 2, James's locked decision #3: SINGULAR ONLY. Plural conditional (-libyśmy/-łybyśmy etc.) is absolutely fenced to b1_conditional_pl after the virile block — not used and not mentioned (no 'plural comes later' line anywhere learner-facing). mógłbym is fenced whole to b1_polite; no gdybym/jeśli...by clauses — simple wishes and soft requests only. oni/one still untaught. Verbs: chcieć (full 6-form singular paradigm, the politeness payoff), kupić + zrobić (perfective twins from a2_aspect, partial spread) — three verbs only, load control. Stem verification: conditional attaches to the 3sg past form, and chciał/chciała (a2_past_rest), kupił/kupiła + zrobił/zrobiła (a2_aspect) are all taught. The 2sg conditionals (chciałbyś, zrobiłabyś) are built on those taught 3sg stems + byś, NOT on chciałeś/zrobiłaś (never taught — verified absent from all blocks); the -ś is anchored on byłeś/byłaś. Distractors all pool-legal. Glosses: chcieć stative → 'would like'; zrobić glossed 'make' consistently in this unit. psa in Użycie = masculine-animate accusative, identical to its taught genitive — the honest acc=gen exception, named here. Both-gender production, (m)/(f) cues as everywhere.

intro.title: Would: built from the past you own
intro.body:
English says would like with a helper word. Polish glues it onto the past form you already know:

1. Take the he/she past form — chciał, chciała.
2. Add -by — chciałby, chciałaby. That is already he/she would like.
3. For I and you, add the byłem endings after the by: -m, -ś — chciałbym, chciałbyś.

Gender costs you nothing new: a man builds on chciał, a woman builds on chciała. The whole conditional is the past tense plus one small syllable.
intro.body_pl: Forma przeszła + by + końcówka z był: chciał + by + m = chciałbym.

intro.title: The polite upgrade
intro.body:
You have said Chcę kawę since your first lessons. It is correct — and direct, like I want coffee.

Chciałbym kawę is the same sentence, one register up: I would like a coffee. Nothing else changes — same word order, same kawę. This is how adults ask for things in shops, cafés and offices.

Poproszę still works for ordering. Chciałbym also covers wishes no waiter can bring: Chciałbym nowy samochód.
intro.body_pl: Chcę kawę = bezpośrednio. Chciałbym kawę = grzecznie.

examples.en: I want coffee. → I would like a coffee. (m)
I want tea. → I would like tea. (f)

intro.title: The same glue on kupić and zrobić
intro.body: The rule is not special to chcieć. Take any past form you know and add the same piece. Here it is on the pair kupić (buy) and zrobić (make):
intro.body_pl: Ta sama zasada: kupił + by = kupiłby, zrobiła + by = zrobiłaby.

intro.title: Wishes and soft requests
intro.body:
The noun picks the form, exactly as it did in the past tense: tata chciałby, mama chciałaby.

And the you-forms give you a soft request: Zrobiłbyś kawę? — Would you make coffee? Softer than an instruction, warmer than silence.
intro.body_pl: Rzeczownik wybiera formę: tata chciałby, mama chciałaby. Zrobiłbyś kawę? = miła prośba.

examples.en: Dad would like a new car.
Would you make coffee? (to a man)
Would you make tea? (to a woman)

quiz.explain: chciał + by + m. The -m after by is the same I-marker as in byłem; without the by it would be plain past chciałem — I wanted.
A woman builds on chciała: chciała + by + m. The feminine -a- sits before the by, not after it.
mama is feminine, so the conditional rides chciała: chciała + by. chciała alone is plain past — she wanted.
tata is a he, so it is kupił + by, with no personal ending after the by — endings after by exist only for I and you.
Same sentence, one register up: chcę → chciałabym for a woman speaking. chciałam would be plain past — I wanted tea.
To a woman: the feminine stem zrobiła + by + ś. The -ś after by is the you-marker from byłaś.
kupił + by. Without the by it is kupił — he bought, already done. The by turns a past fact into a would.
No by = plain past. chciałem is I wanted; chciałbym is I would like. The by is the whole difference.
Anna is a she: kupiła + by. kupiłabym would mean a woman saying I would buy — the -m ties it to I.
ona needs the feminine stem: chciała + by. The gender lives in the past part of the word, before the by.

type_items.explain: chciał + by + m, written as one word. The -m is the I-ending you know from byłem.
Build on the feminine past chciała, then add -bym: chciała-by-m. The -a- comes before the by.
He takes nothing after the by — just chciał + by — exactly as he takes no ending in the past.
Feminine stem zrobiła + byś. The by never changes; only the past part in front of it carries the gender.

use_items.prompt_en: Type: I would like a coffee. (m)
use_items.explain: The polite version of Chcę kawę — same kawę, same order, one register up.

use_items.prompt_en: Type: Dad would like a new car.
use_items.explain: tata is a he despite the -a, so chciałby — the same natural-gender rule as tata był.

use_items.prompt_en: Type: I would buy a house. (m)
Type: I would buy a new bike. (f)
Type: Would you make coffee? (to a man)
use_items.explain: A soft request — the conditional makes the question an invitation, not an order.

Type: My brother would buy a dog.
